reading.title: The Casual Hoodie Visit
reading.intro_zh: 这篇短文把 Lesson 57 的“same person, different treatment”换到现代摄影工作室：一个穿 hoodie 的学生先被轻视，后来工作人员发现他的真实身份和预约背景，态度马上改变。重点练习 hesitate、assistant、serve、the way he was dressed、glancing、scornfully、appointment、eager、with great difficulty 和 appearance。
passage: On Saturday morning, Daniel walked into a small camera studio in a hoodie and old trainers. He hesitated at the counter because the room looked very formal. The assistant noticed the way he was dressed and, glancing at him scornfully, asked him to wait by the door. Daniel politely explained that he had an appointment to test a new school video project, but she hardly listened. A few minutes later, the studio manager came out and greeted him warmly. Daniel was the young prize winner whose film the studio wanted to display. Not realizing who he was, the assistant suddenly felt embarrassed and was eager to serve him. With great difficulty, she set up the heavy lights herself. Daniel thanked her quietly and said that appearance should not decide respect.

questions.question: Why did the assistant judge Daniel at first?
options: She noticed his hoodie and old trainers in a formal-looking studio.
She had already watched his film and disliked it.
Daniel spoke rudely as soon as he arrived.
The studio manager told her not to serve students.
questions.explanation_zh: 短文说 assistant noticed the way he was dressed，并且工作室看起来很正式，所以她根据 Daniel 的 hoodie 和旧运动鞋误判了他。

questions.question: What did Daniel want help with?
options: He wanted to test a new school video project at the studio.
He wanted to buy an expensive coat from the shop window.
He wanted to repair a broken umbrella.
He wanted to ask for directions to another school.
questions.explanation_zh: Daniel 解释自己 had an appointment to test a new school video project，所以他来工作室是为了测试学校视频项目。

questions.question: What new context changed the assistant's attitude?
options: The manager greeted Daniel and showed he was the prize winner whose film would be displayed.
Daniel changed into a suit before speaking again.
The assistant found a ticket in Daniel's pocket.
Another customer complained about the lights.
questions.explanation_zh: manager 出来热情地迎接 Daniel，并说明他是 young prize winner，这个真实身份让 assistant 发现自己误判了。

questions.question: How did the assistant behave differently later?
options: She became eager to serve him and set up the heavy lights herself.
She asked Daniel to leave the studio at once.
She told the manager that Daniel had no appointment.
She laughed at Daniel's school video project.
questions.explanation_zh: 态度变化体现在 was eager to serve him，还 with great difficulty set up the heavy lights herself。

questions.question: What is the main lesson of the passage?
options: Appearance should not decide whether someone receives respect.
Students should never visit camera studios.
Old trainers are better than formal shoes.
People should make assistants do difficult work for fun.
questions.explanation_zh: 结尾 Daniel 平静地说 appearance should not decide respect，呼应 Lesson 57 的核心：不要只根据外表判断一个人。

writing.intro_zh: 今天抓五个 Lesson 57 的外表误判句式：用 Though..., finally... 写犹豫后行动；用 did not like the way...was dressed 写根据衣着判断；用 Glancing at...scornfully 写轻蔑态度；用 Not realizing who...was 写误认身份；用 with great difficulty 写费劲完成的动作。

patterns.title: Though ..., ... finally ...
patterns.source: Though she hesitated for a moment, she finally went in.
patterns.focus_zh: Though 先写犹豫、担心或阻碍，finally 再写人物最终采取行动，适合推动故事开头。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写一个人在门口、柜台前或活动现场犹豫了一下，但最后还是行动了。
patterns.sample: Though Daniel felt nervous at the studio door, he finally walked to the counter.
patterns.tip_zh: Though 后面写让步背景，主句里用 finally 表示“还是做了”。

patterns.title: did not like the way ... was/were dressed
patterns.source: The assistant did not like the way she was dressed.
patterns.focus_zh: 这个句式直接写出“根据穿着判断人”，是 Lesson 57 的社会反差核心。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写某人因为另一个人的穿着而产生错误判断。
patterns.sample: The assistant did not like the way Daniel was dressed for the studio visit.
patterns.tip_zh: the way 后面接完整小句，如 he was dressed 或 they were dressed；不要写成 the way of dressed。

patterns.title: Glancing at ... scornfully, ...
patterns.source: Glancing at her scornfully, he told her that the dress was sold.
patterns.focus_zh: Glancing at...scornfully 把“看了一眼”和“看不起”的态度压缩到句首，画面感很强。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写某人轻蔑地看了别人一眼，然后说出冷淡或不友善的话。
patterns.sample: Glancing at the boy scornfully, the assistant asked him to wait outside.
patterns.tip_zh: 逗号后面要接完整主句；scornfully 是态度，不要把它写成普通 quickly。

patterns.title: Not realizing who ... was, ...
patterns.source: Not realizing who she was, the assistant was eager to serve her.
patterns.focus_zh: 这个句式说明人物因为没有认出身份而改变行为，适合写误会、反转和讽刺。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写某人没有认出另一个人的真实身份，于是做出了错误或夸张的反应。
patterns.sample: Not realizing who Daniel was, the assistant asked him to wait by the door.
patterns.tip_zh: Not realizing who...was 放句首，后面主句写因此发生的行为。

patterns.title: with great difficulty
patterns.source: With great difficulty, he climbed into the shop window.
patterns.focus_zh: with great difficulty 表示动作做得很费劲，能让故事里的服务、搬动、寻找或安装动作更有画面。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写某人费了很大劲完成一个安全但不容易的动作。
patterns.sample: With great difficulty, she moved the heavy lights across the studio.
patterns.tip_zh: 可以把 With great difficulty 放句首；后面写具体动作，避免只写 it was difficult。
